target.rawSql:
WITH days AS (
  SELECT generate_series(
           LEAST(
             (now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')::date - interval '2 years',
             COALESCE(
               (SELECT to_timestamp(min(bucket_start)) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York'
                FROM cex_prices),
               (now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')::date
             )
           ),
           (now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York')::date + interval '14 days',
           interval '1 day'
         ) AS d
)
SELECT
  (d + interval '17 hours') AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York' AS "time",
  (d + interval '2 days 17 hours') AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York' AS "timeEnd",
  'FX market closed' AS text
FROM days
WHERE EXTRACT(DOW FROM d) = 5
ORDER BY 1

description: Raw collected series first, then the regime analytics derived from them. The top row answers 'is there data, and can I see it' for one venue and product at a time, plus what the store holds across every venue. The row below answers what that data says about volatility by session, hour, and weekend. Deliberately shows ONE product at a time rather than overlaying the roster, so it stays legible as currencies are added.

links.title: All data
links.tooltip: Widen the time range to start at this series' own first collected bar, keeping the current venue and product. Exists because the time picker has no such preset — its presets are all relative to now, and none of them can know when collection actually started, so any of them wide enough to hold the whole series also pads the chart with dead space. Drag-selecting on a chart zooms in and there is no equally obvious way back out, so this is the way back out.

links.title: Last 24h
links.tooltip: Narrow to the last day, keeping the current venue and product. At 60s buckets this is the widest window where individual candles are still readable.

panels.description: The raw collected candles for the selected venue and product, straight off the store with no derivation. Shows the full open/high/low/close rather than the close alone, because the range within each bucket is most of what a candle records and plotting only the close discards it. Flip Candle style between Candles and OHLC Bars in the panel editor to change how that range is drawn; set Mode to Both to add the volume histogram beneath. This is the panel to check first: if it is empty, nothing below it means anything. A sparse series with visible gaps is not a fault — a venue emits no candle for a bucket with no trades, so a thinly traded book genuinely looks like scattered marks rather than a continuous run. Over a long window at a small bucket size the candles compress into a solid band; narrow the time range to read individual bars.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  to_timestamp(bucket_start) AS "time",
  "open",
  "high",
  "low",
  "close",
  "volume"
FROM cex_prices
WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
  AND source = ${venue_source:sqlstring}
  AND product_id = ${venue_product:sqlstring}
  AND granularity_secs::text = ${granularity:sqlstring}
ORDER BY bucket_start

panels.title: Price — $venue_product on $venue_source (${granularity}s candles)

panels.description: Everything the store holds, one row per venue and product, independent of the pickers and of the dashboard time range. A table rather than a tile per feed, because the roster grows and a wall of tiles stops being readable well before it stops fitting. The age column is the recency check: a collector that is running keeps it near its own granularity, while a series left behind by a re-pointed or stopped collector shows its age directly. It is rendered as a duration rather than a raw second count, and the two right-hand columns carry fixed widths, because the timestamp beside it is wide enough that in a third-width panel the columns squeeze and the colored age block reads as if it were overlapping its neighbor. Note only one product per collector service is ever current, so several stale rows beside one fresh row is the expected picture today rather than a fault.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  source,
  product_id,
  count(*) AS bars,
  to_timestamp(max(bucket_start)) AS last_bar,
  (extract(epoch FROM now()) - max(bucket_start))::bigint AS age
FROM cex_prices
GROUP BY source, product_id
ORDER BY source, product_id

panels.title: What is in the store

panels.description: Per-bar realized volatility in bps, by hour of day, split into weekday and weekend. This is the vol-ladder's sigma input. Returns are computed between genuinely ADJACENT buckets only: a venue emits no candle for a minute with no trades, and interbank FX leaves a ~48-hour hole every weekend, so a plain window function would bridge those gaps and dump one enormous pseudo-return into a single hour — which reads exactly like a real time-of-day effect. On a sparse book these per-hour cells fall to single digits, where a standard deviation is arithmetic rather than information; check the bar count in the summary table below before trusting a thin cell.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bars AS (
  SELECT bucket_start, close
  FROM cex_prices
  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
    AND source = ${venue_source:sqlstring}
    AND product_id = ${venue_product:sqlstring}
    AND granularity_secs::text = ${granularity:sqlstring}
),
returns AS (
  SELECT
    to_timestamp(bucket_start) AS bucket_ts,
    CASE
      WHEN lag(bucket_start) OVER w = bucket_start - NULLIF(${granularity:sqlstring}, '')::bigint
           AND lag(close) OVER w > 0
           AND close > 0
      THEN ln(close / lag(close) OVER w)
    END AS r
  FROM bars
  WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY bucket_start)
),
classified AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE ${hour_tz:sqlstring})::int AS hour_of_day,
    CASE
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 6
        THEN 'weekend'
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 0
           AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') < 17
        THEN 'weekend'
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 5
           AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') >= 17
        THEN 'weekend'
      ELSE 'weekday'
    END AS regime,
    r
  FROM returns
)
SELECT
  lpad(hour_of_day::text, 2, '0') AS hour,
  stddev_samp(r) FILTER (WHERE regime = 'weekday') * 10000 AS weekday,
  stddev_samp(r) FILTER (WHERE regime = 'weekend') * 10000 AS weekend
FROM classified
GROUP BY hour_of_day
ORDER BY hour_of_day

panels.title: Realized vol by hour ($hour_tz)

panels.description: Per-bar realized volatility in bps, by FX trading session. Answers whether an FX stablecoin inherits the rhythm of its underlying currency's home session or trades on crypto's own flat 24/7 clock. Sessions are local wall-clock windows in each centre, resolved per timestamp, so daylight saving is handled rather than approximated; the hemispheres shift in opposite directions, which no fixed UTC range can express. Sessions OVERLAP and a bar is counted in each it falls in, so the counts sum to more than the total — deliberate, since the London/New York overlap is the highest-liquidity window of the FX day and collapsing it into an exclusive bucket would hide the effect being measured. Compare sessions to each other; do not add them up.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bars AS (
  SELECT bucket_start, close
  FROM cex_prices
  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
    AND source = ${venue_source:sqlstring}
    AND product_id = ${venue_product:sqlstring}
    AND granularity_secs::text = ${granularity:sqlstring}
),
returns AS (
  SELECT
    to_timestamp(bucket_start) AS bucket_ts,
    CASE
      WHEN lag(bucket_start) OVER w = bucket_start - NULLIF(${granularity:sqlstring}, '')::bigint
           AND lag(close) OVER w > 0
           AND close > 0
      THEN ln(close / lag(close) OVER w)
    END AS r
  FROM bars
  WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY bucket_start)
),
sessions (session, tz, open_hour, close_hour) AS (
  VALUES
    ('1 Sydney',   'Australia/Sydney', 8, 17),
    ('2 Tokyo',    'Asia/Tokyo',       9, 18),
    ('3 London',   'Europe/London',    8, 17),
    ('4 New York', 'America/New_York', 8, 17)
)
SELECT
  s.session,
  stddev_samp(r.r) * 10000 AS vol_bps_per_bar
FROM returns r
JOIN sessions s
  ON EXTRACT(HOUR FROM r.bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE s.tz) >= s.open_hour
 AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM r.bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE s.tz) < s.close_hour
 AND EXTRACT(DOW FROM r.bucket_ts AT TIME ZONE s.tz) BETWEEN 1 AND 5
GROUP BY s.session
ORDER BY s.session

panels.title: Realized vol by FX session

panels.description: Weekend against weekday for the selected product. The FX week runs Sunday 17:00 to Friday 17:00 New York time, expressed in that city's local clock so the boundary stays correct across daylight saving. `bars` is the column to read first: it is what tells you whether a volatility number beside it is measurement or arithmetic. `distinct_closes` is texture, NOT a fabrication detector — a genuinely traded weekend carries very few distinct prices, and on this repo's own data weekends show MORE distinct closes per bar than weekdays, so any rule keyed on that ratio fires on honest data.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bars AS (
  SELECT bucket_start, close, high, low
  FROM cex_prices
  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
    AND source = ${venue_source:sqlstring}
    AND product_id = ${venue_product:sqlstring}
    AND granularity_secs::text = ${granularity:sqlstring}
),
regimes AS (
  SELECT
    bucket_start,
    close,
    high,
    low,
    CASE
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM to_timestamp(bucket_start) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 6
        THEN 'weekend'
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM to_timestamp(bucket_start) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 0
           AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM to_timestamp(bucket_start) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') < 17
        THEN 'weekend'
      WHEN EXTRACT(DOW FROM to_timestamp(bucket_start) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') = 5
           AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM to_timestamp(bucket_start) AT TIME ZONE 'America/New_York') >= 17
        THEN 'weekend'
      ELSE 'weekday'
    END AS regime
  FROM bars
),
returns AS (
  SELECT
    regime,
    close,
    high,
    low,
    CASE
      WHEN lag(bucket_start) OVER w = bucket_start - NULLIF(${granularity:sqlstring}, '')::bigint
           AND lag(close) OVER w > 0
           AND close > 0
      THEN ln(close / lag(close) OVER w)
    END AS r
  FROM regimes
  WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY bucket_start)
)
SELECT
  regime,
  count(*) AS bars,
  count(r) AS return_pairs,
  stddev_samp(r) * 10000 AS vol_bps_per_bar,
  avg(abs(r)) * 10000 AS mean_abs_move_bps,
  max(abs(r)) * 10000 AS max_abs_move_bps,
  count(DISTINCT close) AS distinct_closes,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE high = low) AS zero_range_bars
FROM returns
GROUP BY regime
ORDER BY regime

panels.title: Weekend vs weekday

panels.description: Every selected pair on one axis, each indexed to 100 at its first bar inside the visible window. This is the only panel here that reads more than one product at a time, and indexing is what makes that legible: raw closes are not comparable across pairs - EUR-USD sits near 1.08 while EUR-JPY sits near 170 - so an overlay of them is one flat line and one off-scale line. On a percent axis the question 'which of these moved most, and when' has a readable answer. The base is the first bar in the WINDOW rather than the series' first bar ever, so panning or zooming re-bases every series and the comparison always describes the period you are looking at. Pairs come from the Currency picker, so selecting EUR gives every EUR pair this venue carries. A pair with no bar inside the window is dropped rather than drawn flat, so an empty legend entry means 'not collected here', not 'unchanged'.

targets.rawSql:
-- Cross-pair overlay, indexed to 100 at each series' first bar INSIDE the
-- window. Absolute levels are not comparable across pairs -- EUR-USD sits
-- near 1.08 while EUR-JPY sits near 170 -- so an overlay of raw closes is one
-- flat line and one off-scale line, and "which moved most" has no readable
-- answer. Indexing puts every pair on a common percent axis.
--
-- The base is the first bar in the WINDOW, not the series' first bar ever, so
-- panning or zooming re-bases every series and the comparison stays about the
-- period actually on screen.
--
-- Scoped to the selected venue, matching how the rest of this dashboard
-- reads: one venue at a time. Two vendors carrying the same pair would
-- otherwise draw two nearly-identical lines and double the legend for no
-- information.
WITH bars AS (
  SELECT
    product_id,
    bucket_start,
    close
  FROM cex_prices
  WHERE $__unixEpochFilter(bucket_start)
    AND source = ${venue_source:sqlstring}
    AND product_id = ANY (ARRAY[${pairs:sqlstring}]::text[])
    AND granularity_secs::text = ${granularity:sqlstring}
),

base AS (
  -- The earliest bar each pair has in the window, which is its index base.
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (product_id)
    product_id,
    close
  FROM bars
  ORDER BY product_id, bucket_start
)

SELECT
  to_timestamp(b.bucket_start) AS "time",
  b.product_id AS metric,
  -- nullif guards a zero base. Without it one bad series divides by zero and
  -- fails the whole panel rather than just itself.
  100.0 * b.close / nullif(f.close, 0) AS value
FROM bars b
-- INNER, not LEFT: a pair with no bar in the window has no base to index
-- against, and emitting NULLs would add a legend entry that reads as a broken
-- series rather than one this venue does not carry.
INNER JOIN base f ON f.product_id = b.product_id
ORDER BY 1, 2

panels.title: Cross-pair index — $currency pairs on $venue_source (window start = 100)

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT source FROM cex_prices ORDER BY 1
list.description: The venue whose collected series is being shown. Single-select: this dashboard deliberately reads one product at a time rather than overlaying the roster, so that it stays legible as currencies are added.
list.label: Venue source
list.name: venue_source
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT source FROM cex_prices ORDER BY 1

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM cex_prices WHERE source = ${venue_source:sqlstring} ORDER BY 1
list.description: The product to show, listing only what the selected venue actually carries. The filter on the source is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: an unfiltered list offers every product any source has ever written, so it invites selecting a symbol the chosen venue does not and could not quote. The committed default is the product with the densest traded tape, which is the one to verify against when checking that a panel renders.
list.label: Venue product
list.name: venue_product
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM cex_prices WHERE source = ${venue_source:sqlstring} ORDER BY 1

list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT granularity_secs FROM cex_prices WHERE source = ${venue_source:sqlstring} AND product_id = ${venue_product:sqlstring} ORDER BY 1
list.description: Bucket size, in seconds, listing only the values the selected venue and product actually hold. Query-driven rather than a fixed list, and the change is a bug fix: the fixed list offered every bucket size the schema permits while any one venue and product holds exactly one, so five of its six entries selected a silently empty panel that reads as a broken dashboard rather than as absent data. Which five are dead depends on the selection, which is precisely why filtering on the product as well as the source is load-bearing: bucket size varies by venue — the candle venues write 60s buckets and the daily-only FX vendors write 86400s ones — so a list filtered on the source alone would still offer a value the current selection cannot render. On a cold database this variable is empty, which is the honest signal that nothing has been collected yet, and is strictly better than offering a choice that renders nothing. Allowing it to be empty is what forces the two guards every consumer now carries: the filters compare it as text, and the three analytics panels that also do arithmetic on it wrap it so an empty value becomes null instead. Both exist for the same reason — an empty expansion of a bare numeric reference is a SQL parse error rather than an empty result, and a parse error fails before any row is considered, so casting the filter alone would have left those three panels red on a cold database while the other three read as no data. The sibling ingestion dashboard cites exactly that parse error as its reason for hardcoding the list at all; the trade is taken here deliberately and paid for in both places, rather than reversed silently. It is also excluded from URL sync, unlike the two variables above it: a bucket size pinned in a shared or reloaded link can outlive the selection it was valid for and then silently blanks every panel, and since exactly one bucket size exists per venue and product today, there is nothing worth deep-linking. Treat this variable as derived from the other two rather than as state of its own.
list.label: Granularity
list.name: granularity
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT granularity_secs FROM cex_prices WHERE source = ${venue_source:sqlstring} AND product_id = ${venue_product:sqlstring} ORDER BY 1

list.definition:
SELECT DISTINCT legs.c
FROM (
  SELECT i.product_id, i.base AS c FROM instruments i
  UNION ALL
  SELECT i.product_id, i.quote FROM instruments i
) legs
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM instrument_registry r
  WHERE r.source = ${venue_source:sqlstring}
    AND r.product_id = legs.product_id
)
ORDER BY 1
list.description: The currency umbrella: pick one and the Pairs picker below offers every pair with that currency on either leg. This is the selector the dashboard was built without - it reads one product at a time, and the README recorded that selecting by currency needed products tagged by currency family, which was a schema change rather than a dashboard one. That schema landed as the instruments dimension, so this reads the dimension's base and quote legs rather than splitting the product id, which means EURC and EUR are known to be the stablecoin and the fiat of the same currency instead of two unrelated strings. Scoped to the selected venue, for the same reason the Venue product picker is: an unfiltered list invites choosing a currency this venue does not quote, which renders nothing and reads as a broken panel.
list.label: Currency
list.name: currency
list.query:
SELECT DISTINCT legs.c
FROM (
  SELECT i.product_id, i.base AS c FROM instruments i
  UNION ALL
  SELECT i.product_id, i.quote FROM instruments i
) legs
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM instrument_registry r
  WHERE r.source = ${venue_source:sqlstring}
    AND r.product_id = legs.product_id
)
ORDER BY 1

list.description: Whether the Pairs picker offers only pairs currently collecting, or every pair this venue is configured for. Defaults to live only, so the overlay opens on real data rather than on empty series for a pair whose collector is parked - quiet pairs stay reachable, but opt-in. Liveness comes from instrument_liveness, whose staleness bound is chosen by asset class: 72h for a fiat cross so an FX weekend is not mistaken for a dead collector, 48h for the always-open classes. A custom list rather than a query, so it can never be empty.
list.label: Show
list.name: include_quiet

list.definition:
SELECT i.product_id
FROM instruments i
INNER JOIN instrument_liveness l ON l.product_id = i.product_id
WHERE ${currency:sqlstring} IN (i.base, i.quote)
  AND (${include_quiet:sqlstring} = 'all' OR l.is_live)
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM instrument_registry r
    WHERE r.source = ${venue_source:sqlstring}
      AND r.product_id = i.product_id
  )
ORDER BY 1
list.description: The pairs drawn on the cross-pair index panel - every pair carrying the selected Currency on either leg, on the selected venue, filtered by the Show setting. KNOWN COST, and it is measured rather than assumed: instrument_liveness leaves granularity_secs unconstrained, which defeats Postgres's MIN/MAX index transform and range-scans each series, so this query costs about 90ms and grows with cex_prices history. It is on a load-only path - this dashboard sets no auto-refresh - so it is paid once per load rather than continuously. The fix belongs in the view rather than here, and is being carried by the per-source liveness work that rewrites it; measured there at 0.8ms once granularity is constrained. Nothing about this query changes when that lands, it just gets fast.
list.label: Pairs
list.name: pairs
list.query:
SELECT i.product_id
FROM instruments i
INNER JOIN instrument_liveness l ON l.product_id = i.product_id
WHERE ${currency:sqlstring} IN (i.base, i.quote)
  AND (${include_quiet:sqlstring} = 'all' OR l.is_live)
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM instrument_registry r
    WHERE r.source = ${venue_source:sqlstring}
      AND r.product_id = i.product_id
  )
ORDER BY 1

list.definition: SELECT min(bucket_start) * 1000 FROM cex_prices WHERE source = ${venue_source:sqlstring} AND product_id = ${venue_product:sqlstring} AND granularity_secs::text = ${granularity:sqlstring}
list.description: The epoch-millisecond timestamp of the earliest collected bar for the current selection. Hidden, and not a control: it exists so the All data link can widen the time range to exactly where this series starts rather than to a fixed relative window. A fixed window cannot do that job — collection began on a specific date, so any last-N-days range wide enough to hold every bar also pads the chart with empty space to the left of the first bar, and that padding grows by a day every day. The link deliberately ends at now rather than at the last collected bar, so a series that has stopped still shows the gap between its final bar and the present, which is the only on-chart signal that it is dead. Known soft edge: an aggregate with no grouping returns one null row rather than no rows, so on a selection holding nothing this expands to an empty range bound and the link degrades to resetting the time picker with no indication it did. That is accepted rather than fixed, because the case only arises when there is nothing to show anyway.
list.label: Data start
list.name: data_from
list.query: SELECT min(bucket_start) * 1000 FROM cex_prices WHERE source = ${venue_source:sqlstring} AND product_id = ${venue_product:sqlstring} AND granularity_secs::text = ${granularity:sqlstring}

list.description: Wall clock the hour-of-day profile is expressed in. UTC is neutral and right for comparing across currencies; pick a centre's own zone to read the profile as a local trading day. The weekday/weekend split is always computed on the New York FX week regardless of this setting.
list.label: Hour timezone
list.name: hour_tz
